review_candidates.description: About Zuba We're building the global payment network for money moving into, across, and out of the world's emerging markets: instant, transparent, and affordable, with stablecoin rails under the hood. We're backed by multiple unicorn fintech founders and some incredible investors like EWOR, Triple A, Digital Currency Group, Entourage, and Raba. We're early enough that the people joining today define how this company works, and proven enough that the work is real from day one: live partners, live corridors, real money. The problems are hard, the surface area is global, and the prize is a rebuild of how money moves between the fastest-growing markets on earth. We're growing our team to help us shape the future of our industry together. If you see a role that could be a fit for you, please reach out to careers@zuba.com, and let's talk! About the role We're looking for Members of Technical Staff to build the infrastructure our money moves through. The title comes from Bell Labs, where a fresh graduate and a Nobel laureate carried the same one, and we use it the same way. Zuba is deliberately flat: the team is mostly ex-founders, former professional athletes, and generally high achievers, none of that buys anyone rank here. What you did before matters less than what you ship here. We hire problem solvers, not specialists. One month you might be hardening the API institutions use to move money into emerging markets; the next you might be taking our new bet from zero to its first live transaction. Whatever you take on, you own it end to end: product decisions, architecture, partner integrations, rollout to customers, and the client call if something breaks. Two things to know before you apply. First: perhaps unconventional for a financial institution, but we are AI-native. We've realised the goal is no longer to build the car, it's to build the factory that builds the car, and agent orchestration is the default way we build. Few teams run LLMs this deep inside regulated financial infrastructure; we hire engineers who want to work at that edge. Second: we work in person in London, at very high intensity, and we have fun doing it. Mostly type 2 fun: hard while it's happening, the best stories afterwards, with a healthy dose of type 1 along the way. Neither of these is for everyone. Why this might excite you Real money from day one. This isn't a greenfield experiment. Institutional clients move money through what you build, across live corridors, every day. Deep technical problems. Reliable services on top of unreliable providers, each with their own quirks and failure modes. Custody that bridges banking rails and stablecoin rails. Products that work on low-end devices with intermittent connectivity. AI-native engineering. The best tools money can buy, and a team that expects you to multiply your own output with them. You'll work the way the best engineers will work in two years, now. Founder-level exposure. A team of ~15 with no layers. You work directly with the founders, your work shows up in the company's numbers within weeks, and nobody assigns you tickets. What you'll do Build reliable services on unreliable infrastructure. Every payment provider has its own APIs, quirks, and documentation gaps. Clients should never feel any of it. Take products from zero to first transaction. Authentication, virtual accounts, balances, quotes, custody, withdrawals: you'll architect, ship, and iterate on real feedback. Own production. Build the monitoring and resilience layers that catch transaction failures before clients notice. Be on-call, debug live incidents, and talk to the client yourself. Bridge fiat and stablecoin rails. Wallet infrastructure, multi-sig custody, and withdrawal workflows at the intersection of traditional payments and crypto. Design for the real world. Low-end devices, poor connectivity, cost-sensitive users, manual processes. Build things that reinvent the market. Who you are You're a problem solver with agency. You notice what's broken and start moving. "I can't because" becomes "I'll figure out how." You're AI-proficient, genuinely. You ship with AI tooling, you automate yourself out of repetitive work, and you're visibly curious about what's newly possible. If you write most of your code by hand at 2023 speed, we're not the right place for you. You're payments experienced, or payments obsessed. You've run money through production systems before, or you find how money moves fascinating enough to learn fast. Experience preferred, obsession accepted. You're full-stack in practice. TypeScript, React, Node, and Postgres preferred but not rigid. What matters is that you ship production code wherever the problem lives. You ship fast. What you commit to on Monday exists by Friday. You're a clear communicator. Be direct with us. Substance over ego. Bonus points for: Experience with custody/wallet infrastructure or blockchain rails Familiarity with African or emerging-market payments What we offer 💸 Competitive salary + meaningful equity, and we'll show you the maths 🚀 Real ownership: your work shows up in the company's numbers within weeks 🧠 No layers: everyone works directly with the founders 🌍 Paid travel to the markets we serve 🍔 In past 8pm? Dinner and the ride home are on us 🍹 Team off-sites & regular socials Our hiring process We keep it fast and transparent. Intro chat (30 mins) with Max (CTO & Co-Founder): informal discussion about your experience, values, and what you're looking for. An opportunity to get a sense of the role, the team, and how we work. Work trial (2 days, paid). The best way to see if we're a good fit is to work together, and we pay for your time. You'll spend two days with us at our Central London office, building on a real problem alongside the team. Offer. If all goes well, we'll extend an offer and can't wait to welcome you aboard!

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. The IRC leads the way from harm to home. The IRC responds to people’s acute and longer-term needs with integrated programs that improve health and safety, prioritize children’s education, foster economic wellbeing, and empower communities to regain control over their lives. Our work gives rise to some of the most pressing issues facing contemporary humanitarian action, including questions of access, conflict sensitivity, coordination, and impact. The IRC Yemen began its programs in October 2012. Since establishing its presence in the South of Yemen, in the Red Sea Coastal city of Aden, the organization has grown from just an implementing small project to handling large scale emergency and relief operations. Following the war which broke out in Yemen in March of 2015 and the humanitarian disaster, which was crafted by the same, IRC launched one an emergency response program in the southern governorates of Aden, Lahj, Abyan, Shabwah and Al Dhale, and expanded later in Sana’a and Hodeidah in the North. Currently IRC Yemen is operating in eight governorates in the south and north of Yemen through direct programming and through local partnerships, in Health, WASH, Nutrition, Economic Recovery Development, Education, Child Protection, Gender and Women Protection and Empowerment. The International Rescue Committee (IRC) have been working in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) for more than forty years. Today, the IRC has more than 2,200 staff working across the region, including in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, and Yemen to support those affected by some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises. Scope Of Work The Field Manager leads IRC operations and program support in Shabwah and Abyan, ensuring effective, compliant, and secure field activities. The role represents IRC with authorities, communities, partners, and coordination forums to strengthen relationships and support program delivery. The position also supervises field staff, oversees administrative functions, and contributes to strategic decision-making. Job Summary The Field Manager oversees supporting the programs and operations in the sub-field office of Shabwah, and will also cover the same in Abyan. Reporting to the Field Coordinator, the incumbent shall be representing IRC with government line ministries, counterparts, local communities and stakeholders as well as taking part and representing IRC in other forums, such as OCHA coordination meetings. This position is a member of the extended Senior Management Team and participates in all meetings and decision-making forums within IRC in line with his/her Job Description. Working Relations Position Reports to: Field Coordinator Position directly supervises: SC Officer, Humanitarian Access Officer, Finance/Admin Assistant. This position will also provide day-to-day administrative supervision for the most senior program staff from each sector. Coordinate with Finance, Admin and program departments to ensure integrated internal controls, timely payment of vendors and full, auditable support documentation. Continuously monitor security developments in Shabwah and Abyan Governorates to ensure the security and safety of IRC staff, programs and assets. Manage field-level security incidents in close cooperation with the Humanitarian Access Coordinator, Field Coordinator and Country Director as required. Ensure that all IRC premises — including the Shabwah sub-field office, in consultation with the Senior IT Officer on IT-related standards — meet IRC standards, and recommend improvements where necessary. Routinely communicate, coordinate and plan with the respective requesting staff/programs regarding the order and delivery of supplies. Ensure that IRC has adequate storage capacity for program supplies. Oversee vehicle operations and usage for the smooth and safe running of the programs. Lead on new facility identification and selection, when required. Manage initial set-up, if applicable. Maintain office records and disseminate information and correspondence between the field office and capital offices. Program Support Provide consistent and constructive support to all program departments in Shabwah and Abyan Governorates. Follow up with the sub-field office program staff to ensure quality programming is carried out for both direct implementation and partner implementation, and that IRC and donor expectations are met. Perform regular program site visits to ensure required progress and quality in implementation of activities. Communicate and coordinate with capital-based Program Sector Leads to address any issues affecting quality or timeline of program activities. Closely follow up on the work of Project Managers and Officers to ensure they are well informed of the activities and funds they are responsible for. Promote IRC's image and work, ensuring IRC activities are clearly marked with IRC and donor logos, where applicable. Partnership Responsibilities Work with Operations Management Team colleagues to support partners' capacity, ensuring adherence to IRC processes and agreed donor guidelines. Actively participate in Partnership Cycle Management, including partnership project opening, review, and closing meetings, capturing effective operational practices and lessons learned for future partnerships. Where IRC procures on behalf of a partner, ensure a partner procurement plan is agreed with the partner and the relevant technical lead at the outset of the partnership agreement, and that project budgets reflect fair market value. Coordination Represent IRC at all forums and at the inter-cluster coordination meetings chaired by UN OCHA. Representing IRC in front of governmental authorities and local communities. Convey information on IRC program activities and criteria and pass community needs and requests to program coordinators. Coordinate, support and oversee the work of IRC's local partner(s). Staff Management Establish and preserve close, open, ethical and professional working relationships among staff, and between staff and communities. Work towards strengthening staff's team spirit by demonstrating good leadership. Address any issues or misunderstandings which arise within the framework and spirit of IRC policies and rules of professional conduct. Support staff in the implementation of personnel policies, including performance evaluation, staff development, and disciplinary measures. Ensure attendance and leave management of all staff assigned to the Shabwah and Abyan sub-field offices, in close coordination with their capital-based managers. Compliance Ensure adherence to IRC policies and procedures across all operations departments, including Supply Chain, Humanitarian Access, People & Culture, Finance and IT. Ensure health, safety and security protocols are followed at all times, taking timely corrective action as required and in consultation with the Field Coordinator and SMT. Ensure that IRC SOPs and contingency plans are kept up to date and respected and enforce the same in the Shabwah and Abyan sub-field offices and throughout IRC implementation areas. Promptly inform the Field Coordinator of any areas of concern regarding potential or suspected violations of policies and procedures. Strategy and Program Approach Member of PWG, and co-responsible for delivering the functions of the PWG. Contribute to robust stakeholder analysis processes stakeholder analysis processes that enable the Strategy Action Plan (SAP) and each program design to be based on how we can best support, reinforce and complement local civil society, government and private sector actors. Member of PWG, and co-responsible for delivering the functions of the PWG, with respect to the relevant geographical area. Program Delivery Participate in due diligence processes and collaborative partnership risk management as appropriate. Engage in program design processes including providing input into partnership opportunities. Participate in PCM, including to review successes, challenges, and lessons learned with the partner, and capturing effective finance practices for future partnerships. Assist with any security related local partner issues and coordinate with the partner on safe access. Coordination and Feedback Assist in resolving any local partner issues at the field level, ensuring that any communication is coordinated and consistent with that of the relevant technical coordinator and Partnership Lead, including addressing partner feedback and concerns. Contribute to local liaison and coordination with relevant partners, in close coordination with technical and partnership leads. In coordination with technical and partner leads, support liaison with local authorities as it relates to partnerships. Soft Skills And Competencies Customer- and client-centered, with a service-oriented mindset and attitude. Energetic, with good networking, interpersonal and communication skills. Excellent problem-solving skills, creativity and flexibility. Ability to work independently. Ability to handle pressure. Detail-oriented and professionally patient. Negotiation and diplomacy, including the ability to navigate politically sensitive conversations and resolve disputes with authorities and stakeholders. Sound judgment and risk analysis in security-sensitive contexts. Cross-functional coordination and organizational agility, with the ability to manage competing priorities across departments not directly supervised. People leadership and coaching, including staff development, feedback, and performance management. Cultural and contextual sensitivity is specific to the Shabwah/Abyan operating environment. Language Skills: Fluency in English and Arabic to communicate clearly and effectively. Computer Skills: MS Office – Very good MS Word, MS Excel, MS Outlook. Working Environment: Based in Ataq, Shabwah, with frequent travel to Abyan and some travel to Aden. IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, age, marital status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. IRC strives to build a diverse and inclusive team at all levels who as individuals, and as a group, embody our culture statement creating a working environment characterized by critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity for us to achieve our aspirations as a team and deliver the best possible services to our clients. Gender Equality: IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. Commitment to Client Responsiveness: By committing to Client-Centered Programming, at the IRC Yemen, we place the people we serve - our clients - at the center of our programming and services.
